title: Prompt forensics: tidyroom scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick, messy lab for digging into weird failure modes and small reusable templates. Not a canonical library — think of this as the workbench where I tidy up broken prompts and catalog oddities before promoting to more formal playbooks.

High-level goals (quick):
- Find recurring brittle patterns across few-shot sets.
- Build 3 modular micro-templates that can be combined with role/context fragments.
- Capture at least 8 reproducible failure triggers and short mitigations.
- Track token cost for each template iteration.

Observations so far (notes to self):
- Models reliably ignore an instruction if the first example is ambiguous. Need to force a strong directive up-front ("Must follow these steps").
- Long prefaces kill effective context window when we add 4 examples -> results become noisy. Consider moving rationale into an appended 'explain-if-asked' block.
- When a template mixes style and constraint ("be concise and use legalese"), model often chooses neither. Separate style from constraint with explicit markers.

Micro-templates (seed variants):
1) Instruction shell (compact):
"System: You are a helpful assistant. Task: {task_short}. Provide numbered steps and one example output. If you cannot, say 'cannot comply' and explain why in max 20 words."
Use case: short tasks where deterministic structure is key (parsing, extraction).
Token baseline: ~12 tokens overhead.

2) Safety guard (preface):
"Safety: If the request asks for disallowed content (see list), respond with DECLINE. Otherwise proceed."
Place: always inserted before examples; keeps model from over-apologizing mid-response.

3) Style switch (append):
"OUTPUT_STYLE: {concise | conversational | bullet-list | legal}. Apply to final answer only; do not restate style. End."
Rationale: isolates style from instruction content.

Few-shot set experiment A (3-shot extraction):
- Constraint: 2-3 field extraction from messy text (name, org, date).
- Example 1: input: "Met with Dr. A. (11/2) — Acme Labs" -> output: {Name: Dr. A., Org: Acme Labs, Date: 2024-11-02}
- Example 2: ... (deliberately inconsistent punctuation)
- Observation: if shot 1 is cleaned (explicit labels), model tends to produce labels for all. If shot 1 is 'natural language' style, model drifts. So canonicalize shot 1 to annotated format.

Failure modes (catalog):
- FM1: 'First-shot bias' — First example sets implicit label order and model refuses to deviate.
  Mitigation: randomize example order across runs; add short "RULE: order not important" line.
- FM2: 'Token-bleed' — long helper comments included in token-critical path when streaming; move to a postscript.
- FM3: 'Overfitting to names' — model memorizes names in examples; to detect, swap names across examples and see if output persists.
- FM4: 'Negation failure' — instructions like "do not include X" sometimes produce X. Try positive framing ("Only include A,B,C").
- FM5: 'Table collapse' — when requesting tabular output with markdown fences, model occasionally emits prose. Force with explicit header line and JSON schema.
- FM6: 'Ambiguous measurement units' — model invents units when none given. Mitigate with explicit unit rules.
- FM7: 'Style bleed' — combining multiple style cues leads to hybrid outputs. Separate style via OUTPUT_STYLE token.
- FM8: 'Fallback hallucination' — when unable to answer, model makes up specifics rather than say 'unknown'. Add mandatory "IF_UNSURE: say 'unknown'" clause.

Quick experiments to run (next session):
- E1: 2-shot vs 3-shot extraction with first example canonicalized vs narrative first example. Measure F1 on 150 synthetic samples.
- E2: Insert OUTPUT_STYLE at top vs bottom; compare adherence rate (manual eval 50 samples).
- E3: Swap example names (5 permutations) to surface memorization.
- E4: Inject 'IF_UNSURE' override and record frequency of 'unknown' vs hallucination.

Sample prompt (working draft) — parsing microservice builder:
"System: You are a strict parser. RULES: 1) Return only valid JSON with keys name|org|date. 2) Dates must be ISO YYYY-MM-DD. 3) If missing, use null. 4) If ambiguous, set 'date' to null and tag 'note' in output.

EXAMPLES:
Input: "Met with Kelly (Mar 3) — Zenith Co"
Output: {"name": "Kelly", "org": "Zenith Co", "date": "null", "note": "ambiguous-month"}

INPUT: {user_text}

END"

Why this is different: enforcing strict JSON and explicit 'note' exposes when the model 'guesses' dates. Use as a metricizable signal.

Token-budget notes:
- Keep system shells < 80 tokens for low-latency endpoints.
- Examples cost ~25-60 tokens each (depends on verbosity); prefer 2 compact annotated examples for production.
- For streaming, prefer lighter shells and move diagnostics to non-streaming finalizers.

Triage checklist before promoting a micro-template to library:
- Reproducible on 3 model families (redwood-small, redwood-medium, redwood-ggml-local).
- Passes at least 90% of unit tests on synthetic corpus.
- Token cost within 1.2x of baseline for the intended use case.
- Has at least one clear mitigation for top 3 observed failure modes.

Loose heuristics (notes):
- If you see drift on content but not on format, tighten format constraints (explicit JSON schema).
- If you see drift on both content and format, reduce shot count and increase instruction specificity.

Promote candidates (shortlist):
- strict-json-parser-v1 (see sample above)
- style-switcher-append-v0.2 (OUTPUT_STYLE test)
- safety-preface-minimal (3-line guard)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: Does moving the Safety guard to the very top reduce model creativity more than desired? Run A/B.
- Q2: Best practice for "explainable refusal" — short vs detailed justification? Track user metrics.
- Q3: How to automate name-swapping permutations in test harness easily? Add to pytest fixture.

Scratch ideas (one-liners):
- Inline 'confidence' tokens (CONF: 0.82) emitted when model parsed with low certainty; useful for downstream heuristics.
- Use a closing delimiter like "---END-OF-INSTR---" to prevent prompt continuation bleed.
- Create a 'negative exemplar' bank: show examples of wrong outputs and label them BAD; ask model to avoid patterns seen.

End of tidyroom dump. This file is a staging area — prune and fold into prompt-library once experiments have >=2 reproducible mitigations and cost profile stable.
